 State Tax Service: the deadline for replacing cash registers is 30 November
 By 30 November this year, taxpayers are required to decommission and deregister nine types of cash register equipment that have reached the end of their service life and replace them with devices connected to the ‘Electronic Sales Monitoring’ automated information system. 
 15 November 2026 
 Tatiana Sichirliiscaia

 The State Tax Service reminds taxpayers that 30 November 2026 marks the expiry date for the use of nine models of cash register equipment (CRE). Obsolete devices have been removed from the Unified Register of CRE by a decision of the Interdepartmental Commission on Cash Register Equipment.
 As there is little time left before this deadline, the State Tax Service recommends selecting suitable equipment in advance, depending on the sector of activity. The taxpayer must then submit an application to the Technical Support Centre to register the equipment in the ‘Electronic Sales Monitoring’ information system (SIA ‘MEV’).
 This system provides real-time information on transactions carried out using cash register equipment, as well as sales monitoring and risk analysis.
 The replacement of cash registers must be carried out in compliance with the requirements for the documentation and storage of fiscal memory. According to the regulations, users are obliged to retain the memory and/or SD cards for six years.
 Furthermore, equipment may only be replaced by those technical support centres and exclusive distributors of cash registers that hold the relevant registration certificate.
